implementation_notes: The stdlib supplies the structure: queue.Queue (bounded via maxsize) is the activation queue, a threading.Thread running a dequeue loop is the scheduler, and concurrent.futures.Future is the result handle - with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1).submit(fn, ...) as the one-line version that serializes execution and returns the future in one call. Only the worker thread touches the servant, so it needs no locks. Because of the GIL this buys decoupling and ordering for I/O-bound or blocking servants, not CPU parallelism.
pitfalls: ThreadPoolExecutor's queue is unbounded; a caller that outruns the servant grows memory - a queue.Queue(maxsize=n) with a worker loop gives back-pressure instead.
Blocking on Future.result() from a task already inside the same single-worker pool deadlocks.
The GIL prevents parallel CPU execution; move CPU-bound servants to multiprocessing or a C extension.

variants.name: asyncio.Queue + single consumer task
variants.idiom_name: asyncio.Queue + one consumer task + awaitable future
variants.implementation_notes: In asyncio code the same roles are played by asyncio primitives: asyncio.Queue(maxsize=n) is the activation queue, one task running an async-for loop is the scheduler, and the awaitable returned by the proxy (or an explicit asyncio.Future) is the Future. Serialization comes from having exactly one consumer task; the servant must never block the loop, so either it uses async I/O or the proxy pushes blocking calls through loop.run_in_executor. Choose this over the thread form when the application is already asynchronous.
variants.code_sketch:
async def serve(requests, servant):
    while True:                                    # scheduler: one at a time
        method, args, fut = await requests.get()
        try:
            fut.set_result(await method(servant, *args))
        except Exception as exc:
            fut.set_exception(exc)

async def put(self, msg):                          # proxy
    fut = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
    await self._requests.put((MQServant.put_i, (msg,), fut))
    return await fut
pitfalls: A blocking call (time.sleep, requests, plain file I/O) inside the consumer stalls the entire event loop.
An unbounded asyncio.Queue hides overload; pass maxsize and await put() for back-pressure.
An exception that escapes the consumer loop stops the object while callers wait forever - complete each future and restart or fail fast.
